title: What If Every New City Building Were Made of Wood?
subject: wooden skyscraper

scenes.text: What if every new building were made of wood? Cities could turn into carbon vaults.
Making steel and concrete is carbon-intensive. Wood does the opposite and locks carbon into the beams.
One study estimates timber buildings could store 10 to 68 million tons of carbon every year.
Wood towers already stand. Norway's Mjosa Tower has 18 floors.
Tests of glue-laminated beams and cross-laminated timber showed fire resistance in buildings up to 18 stories.
So the real limit isn't fire. It's whether forests can keep up.
